The Two Palettes

Two Palettes, One Voice

Issue Nº 01
Editor's
Note
"Two palettes, twenty-four templates, one rule: nothing gets posted that doesn't already belong. This issue walks through how a five-tone forest palette and a four-tone bright green became a feed system a fashion account can run for a year without a single off-brand tile."
Boss — the editorial register
Forest · Pine · Sage · Stone · Chalk
Verde — the commercial register
Pine Dark · Emerald · Verde · Moss

Five tones carry Boss, running from a near-black forest down to a pale chalk — wide enough to hold moody, low-light photography without ever drifting warm. Verde trims that down to four brighter greens, built for a feed that leans commercial and daylight-shot rather than editorial.

Neither pack borrows a tone from outside its own range. That's the whole trick: a photo that's slightly off still reads as on-brand, because the palette was chosen to be forgiving in exactly the direction real photography drifts.

Boss / Verde Feed Systems

The Brief
01 — The Brief

Anatomy of a Locked Palette

The brief was never "design a banner." It was a full Instagram feed system for a fashion and lifestyle account — quote cards, product close-ups, editorial covers and testimonial mockups, all built to share one visual grammar. Locking the palette first meant every later decision, down to the smallest caption card, had somewhere to sit.

Two packs came out of that brief. Boss runs five tones from a near-black forest to a pale chalk, tuned for a moodier, editorial feed. Verde runs four brighter greens, better suited to a lighter, more commercial feed — same grammar, different register.

"Twenty-four tiles, four repeating template types — the photo changes, the system never does."

Each pack opens with its palette and a row of content-format icons — grid, Reels, IGTV, camera — signalling the kit was scoped for more than static tiles from day one.

Scope of Work
04 — Scope of Work

What I Did & What I Didn't

Written plainly, for the record: this is the full extent of the design work behind Boss and Verde, and exactly where that work stops. No handle was supplied for either pack, so no live account was ever touched.

What I Did — as Designer
✓Designed two complete Instagram feed template systems — Boss (5-tone forest palette) and Verde (4-tone bright palette), 12 templates each, 24 total.
✓Selected and locked each color palette so every tile in a grid reads as one cohesive brand.
✓Built four repeating template types — quote card, product close-up, editorial cover, profile/testimonial mockup — so any pack scales to new photos.
✓Planned the content-format icon row (grid / Reels / IGTV / camera) for multi-format use.
✓Built the phone mockups in this issue, simulating how each grid would look live, for presentation purposes only.
✓Delivered both packs as ready-to-edit Canva files for a client or account manager to populate.
What I Did Not Do
—Did not manage, operate, or have login access to any live Instagram account.
—Did not create, schedule, or publish a single post.
—Did not write final captions, hashtags, or copy — the "coloque seu texto aqui" slots are intentional placeholders for whoever runs the account.
—Did not shoot or select the photography shown — template images are placeholders for demonstration only.
—Did not provide growth, engagement, community management, or wider social strategy — visual template design only.
—No account handle was ever supplied, so no live profile was connected to this work at any point.
This page reflects the complete scope of work for Boss / Verde. Any activity not listed above — including posting, captioning or account management — was performed by someone else, or has not yet happened.
